title: [YouPass Collect] - Electricity production in France by source: 1980 - 2012
prompt: The graph shows electricity production (in terawatt hours) in France between 1980 and 2012. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the amount of electricity generated from four different sources in France over a 32-year period, from 1980 to 2012.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while nuclear power experienced a dramatic surge to become the dominant energy source, thermal power declined considerably despite recording the highest figure at the beginning. In addition, hydroelectric power fluctuated within a narrow range, and renewables only began to show notable growth towards the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the two sources with the most significant changes, in 1980, thermal power was the leading source of electricity at 120 TW-h, nearly double that of nuclear power, which stood at 65 TW-h. However, nuclear energy subsequently experienced a remarkable rise, climbing steadily to reach a peak of 430 TW-h in 2005, before dropping slightly to 405 TW-h in 2012. In contrast, thermal power saw a sharp decline, falling to a low of just 35 TW-h by 1993. It then recovered slightly, fluctuating between 40 and 58 TW-h, and ended the period at 42 TW-h.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the other two energy sources, hydroelectric power started at 70 TW-h in 1980, a figure similar to that of nuclear power at the time, while virtually no renewable electricity was produced that year. Throughout the period, hydroelectric power fluctuated within a range of 48 to 78 TW-h, before ending at 55 TW-h in the final year. Renewables, on the other hand, remained negligible until around 2008, after which they increased noticeably, reaching 25 TW-h by the end of the period.
